About me

Tasneea Zahra

Research Collaborator · KUET EEE graduate

Hi there, glad you stopped by! I’m an EEE graduate from KUET, where I completed my B.Sc. in 2025.

I’m passionate about research, especially reinforcement learning, efficient LLM training, multimodal learning, and computer vision.

That interest led me to collaborate with Prof. Ser-Nam Lim at the University of Central Florida and fellow researchers at other institutions. Together, we worked on PrePO, which aims to reduce optimizer steps and training time while maintaining performance. Read our paper submitted to ICLR 2027 ↗

Selected work

Publications & preprints

01
012026

Preprint · Submitted to ICLR 2027

Skip What You Can Predict: Predictive Repositioning for Policy Optimization for Efficient LLM Training

I. N. Swapnil, A. Saha, T. Zahra, T. A. Khan, M. A. Haque, & S.-N. Lim

PrePO extrapolates from two observed same-batch optimizer updates to a farther point on the trajectory, then corrects it. It matches baseline performance with fewer optimization steps and less wall-clock time; gains also carry over to supervised fine-tuning.

022025

Conference publication · BECITHCON 2025

Trans-SPAnet: A Unified Transformer–CNN Architecture with Enhanced Boundary Optimization for Polyp Segmentation

A hybrid CNN–Transformer for polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images. Spatial-context preservation blocks retain fine detail, a Transformer decoder models long-range context, and boundary-aware optimization sharpens polyp contours.

View on IEEE Xplore ↗
Read abstract

Accurate segmentation of anatomical structures in medical images, such as polyps, remains a critical, yet challenging task due to the variability in appearance, low contrast, and irregular boundaries. While U-Net-based architectures demonstrate strong local feature extraction, they often lack the capability of global context modeling. On the other hand, transformer-based models capture long-range dependencies but struggle with local detail preservation, which requires a huge amount of data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel hybrid CNN-transformer U-Net architecture that integrates spatial pyramid convolution blocks (SPCB) and spatial pyramid pooling blocks (SPPB) for multi-scale local feature extraction, with a transformer bottleneck for global context understanding. Furthermore, we introduce a boundary-sensitive loss function to enhance performance at object boundaries, a known problem in conventional approaches. Our decoder employs refined transformer fusion modules to reconcile semantic gaps across different scales. We evaluate our model on Kvasir-SEG dataset for polyp segmentation, which performs 2-3% better than existing baseline segmentation models. The results demonstrate that our architecture performs better than existing CNN-only or transformer-only models in medical image segmentation.

Selected projects

Building across research and engineering

Qwen3-VL · GRPO · vLLM · Jun 2025 – Present

Bangla OCR: Progressive Training of a Compact VLM

  • Built a Bangla document OCR model for handwritten and printed text using progressive vision-language alignment, supervised OCR, and reinforcement learning with text-accuracy rewards.
  • Created an automated data engine using multi-model consensus, synthetic degraded pages, and image-to-image self-verification.
  • Served the model with vLLM and added PyTorch and ONNX deployment backends.

Gemini File Search · LangGraph · RAG

Multimodal RAG Assistant for Scientific Papers

  • Designed a PDF retrieval pipeline that uses text, tables, and figures and grounds answers in cited passages.
  • Built a LangGraph agent to route queries to paper summaries, targeted questions, or citation lookup.
  • Added persistent multi-session chat and per-user document libraries.

Arduino · G-code · Stepper motors

Image-to-Drawing CNC Plotter

  • Built a drawing machine with X/Y stepper motors and a servo to lift the pen.
  • Converted images to vector toolpaths and G-code; simulated the circuit in Proteus before assembly.

Verilog · Quartus · Altera FPGA

FPGA-Based Arithmetic Logic Unit

  • Designed a multi-bit ALU supporting arithmetic, logic, and shift operations with carry, zero, and overflow flags.
